chunks: From him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Daylam, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man drinks wine, then spits, and his spit lands on my garment.' He said: 'It is not [impure].'

key_terms.الْخَمْرَ: Wine (the specific drink, often used for impurity rulings)

ai.seo_question: Is the spit of a person who drinks wine considered impure in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the consumption of wine does not inherently render a person's bodily fluids impure (*najis*), specifically ruling that their spit is pure. This highlights the Shia juristic distinction between the internal state of the drinker and the physical purity of their excretions, contrasting with views that might consider the drinker impure due to the substance itself. The ruling emphasizes that the impurity of wine is primarily in the liquid itself, not necessarily transferring to all bodily outputs of the consumer.
